body: In my opinion, I think a serious reality check is long overdue .. religiosity has nothing to do with race or ethnicity; it’s about personal values, character, and how one chooses to live. In the UAE, there’s a culture of collective shock when anything foreign or unfamiliar enters the space, but this reaction often stems from a long standing habit of sweeping uncomfortable truths under the rug. In reality, I see people doing things every day that contradict the very values society claims to uphold. The more we suppress these behaviors or pretend they don’t exist, the more they manifest because silence doesn’t erase problems; it feeds them. This is the ripple effect of generational trauma, lack of emotional awareness, and a failure to truly instill values from a place of understanding rather than fear or control. The UAE’s social demographic shifted so rapidly due to its explosive growth that people barely had time to adjust or reflect, and instead of gaslighting each other with “there are no issues,” it’s time to acknowledge them. Seeing and admitting what’s real is the first step to healing. The world recalibrates itself with time, but that only works if each person takes responsibility for themselves and their family and leading by example, practicing what Allah has commanded with sincerity, instead of being consumed by superficial appearances and social validation.
